subject: Velora Health — Renewal: reserved GPU capacity & throughput forecast
messages:

Cc: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@velorahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal coming up — need guidance on capacity for Q2/Q3

Hi Sean —

Our renewal for Redwood Dedicated is up on Feb 28. Q4 usage surprised us: peak API QPS doubled and token consumption climbed ~2.4x vs. Q3. We're forecasting continued growth as we roll the new triage assistant into more clinics.

Can you help with: 1) an example capacity plan (QPS -> GPUs) for a 3–6 month commit; 2) recommended reserved pool size vs. burst; and 3) any impact to SLA/throughput guarantees if we add instances mid-term?

I've attached our anonymized usage export (velora_usage_q4_2025.csv). Would prefer a short call next week (Carlos and I are available Tue/Wed morning PST).

—Emma
Director of Product Operations
Velora Health

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — need guidance on capacity for Q2/Q3

Emma — thanks for the data and heads up (and hi Carlos). We dug into the CSV and sketched a renewal-focused capacity plan. High level answers up front:

- We can support your projected 2–3x token growth with a blend of reserved pool + burst capacity; recommended starting point is +32 A100-equivalent GPUs in reserved pool (explained below).
- For SLAs, adding GPUs mid-term is supported; throughput guarantees can be updated during renewal or via a mid-term change order — lead time for procurement + provisioning is typically 7–10 business days for Dedicated pools.
- We recommend a quarterly re-eval for the first 3 quarters post-rollout and an opt-in autoscaling buffer of 20% for burst.

I'll summarize the forecast and our sizing assumptions. Neha — tagging you for pricing/terms and whether to propose a 12-month commit with a 6-month ramp. Marissa — can you add ops notes on KV cache pinning and multi-model routing to reduce peak GPU needs?

Proposed next steps: quick 30 min sync Tue 20 Jan 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 21 Jan 09:00–09:30 PT.

—Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Emma/Carlos — quick commercial note ahead of the call: given the growth profile, we usually structure renewals as a stepped reserved pool: 1) Months 0–3: commit 24 GPUs, 2) Months 4–6: commit 32 GPUs, 3) month 7+: reassess (option to convert burst into reserved). That keeps monthly spend aligned to utilization while giving predictable baseline throughput.

Pricing: I can draft a renewal with 12-month term and a 4-month ramp discount (10% off baseline unit price during months 1–4). If you'd prefer a 24-month with larger discount, we can model that.

I'll put numbers into HubSpot right after our sync.

—Neha
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 10:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — need guidance on capacity for Q2/Q3

Thanks everyone — good call. Summary and operational recommendations from our session:

Summary of Velora forecast (from CSV + on-call):
- Current peak QPS: ~280 (p95 spikes to 420)
- Avg token/sec at peak: ~12k tokens/sec across applications
- Expected growth after rollout: +2.5x peak QPS by end of Q2

Sizing assumptions used:
- Model family: medium-sized decoder (ca. 30B) with KV cache working set on GPU memory; generation average of ~85 tokens/request; typical latency target p95 <= 450ms per request.
- Measured tokens/sec per A100-eq GPU (in your workload profile after batching & KV cache pin): 450–520 tokens/sec sustained; burst throughput up to 900 tokens/sec with aggressive batching and multi-instance routing.

Recommended reserved pool at renewal (numbers are conservative, aligned with your 99th percentile targets):
- Baseline reserved: 28 A100-eq GPUs to cover steady-state 95th percentile with 20% autoscale buffer.
- Burst credit / soft-cap: additional 12 GPUs available for burst (pay-as-you-go or short-term burst contract).
- Suggested guardrails: prefix cache pinning for top 40% of requests, request-level priority routing for latency-critical paths.

Operational notes:
- If Velora wants a firm throughput guarantee for a specific route (e.g., triage/urgent), we recommend isolating that route onto a smaller reserved pool (6–8 GPUs) to avoid noisy-neighbor issues.
- Lead time: 7–10 business days for GPU allocation; capacity add mid-term can be codified as a change order.

I'll attach the micro-benchmark report for your exact model family (send separately if you want the raw traces).

—Marissa
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

Attachment: (sent separately upon request)

Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — need guidance on capacity for Q2/Q3

Thanks — that sizing matrix is helpful. Couple of follow-ups from Velora: 1) Can you convert Marissa's recommended baseline (28 GPUs + 12 burst) into expected p95 latency numbers for our triage route at 75/85/95th percentiles? 2) Will the proposed reserved pool support KV cache pinning for our two heaviest prefixes (they are ~60% of traffic together)?

Also, Emma asked me to confirm whether the 7–10 business day lead time includes additional networking setup on our side (proof-of-concept dedicated VPC was already provisioned).

We can sign a renewal with those numbers if we can get a written throughput guarantee for the isolated triage route and a 30-day SLA credit window for missed throughput SLOs.

—Carlos
Sr. Infra PM, Velora Health

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@velorahealth.com>, Emma Li <emma.li@velorahealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 18:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — need guidance on capacity for Q2/Q3

Carlos/Emma — great questions. Short answers in-line, then proposed deliverables by EOD Fri:

1) Latency estimates for triage route at the target reserved sizing: our lab bench (with similar model and batching) predicts p75=220ms, p85=330ms, p95=470ms on a dedicated 6-GPU isolated pool for that route. We'll produce a short SLA appendix with those numbers embedded and a measurable signal (route-level token throughput and p95 latency) to tie to credits.

2) KV cache pinning: yes — the reserved pool will support pinning top prefixes; with your two prefixes accounting for ~60% of traffic, the effective tokens/sec per GPU increases to ~640 tokens/sec sustained in practice. We'll put the cache pin plan in the ops runbook.

3) Lead time: 7–10 business days is for pure infra provisioning. Networking tasks on your side (VPC peering, firewall rules) are typically parallel effort—if your infra team confirms the VPC peering is ready we can do provisioning within 5 business days.

Deliverables by EOD Fri 23 Jan: 1) a 2-page renewal summary (numbers + terms) for signature, 2) SLA appendix for the triage route with measurable SLOs and credit formula, 3) an ops checklist for KV cache pinning and routing. I'll loop legal if we need specific contract language on credits.

If that works I'll circulate the DocuSign link for the renewal and a change-order template.

—Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
